provenance.source: software defaults, not calibrated against measured shots
limitations: No measured shot has been fitted yet: treat every value here as a placeholder.
kozeny_constant and extraction_rate_ref_s are the two dominant knobs; fit them first.
Estimated TDS and extraction yield are engineering outputs, not flavor scores.
notes_on_kozeny_constant: The textbook Kozeny-Carman shape constant is about 180. This file uses 4.0e6.

The four orders of magnitude are not a unit error: they absorb everything a single representative particle diameter cannot express in a real espresso bed - fines filling the voids between coarse particles, tamping compaction, and internal particle porosity. A textbook 180 with d_p = 350 um predicts a permeability near 1e-10 m^2, while espresso pucks measure nearer 1e-15 m^2.

This is stated here rather than buried in the code because the guide forbids hiding empirical tuning behind unexplained constants. It is the first coefficient that should be replaced by a fit to measured shots, and doing so will likely change its magnitude again.
